clue.text: Diminishing intelligence seen as a national problem

definitions.text: Diminishing intelligence seen as a national problem

parts.words: Diminishing intelligence seen as a national problem
parts.note: read literally it sounds like a country getting dimmer; really it is the loss of clever people emigrating abroad

explanation.surface: A commentator worries that the country is getting collectively less clever.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests falling IQ, but the phrase means the emigration of skilled and educated people, which reduces a nation's stock of talent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for the emigration of a country's educated and skilled workers, a recognised national worry.

clue.text: Call for attention to burn

definitions.meaning: a summons made by a nod or gesture, as in being at someone's call
burn is a northern British and Scottish word for a stream or brook

explanation.surface: A gesture summoning someone over to a little stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Burn is not fire here: in Scotland and northern England a burn is a small stream, and so is this word in northern dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a summoning gesture, and a northern English word for a brook or stream.

clue.text: Almost turn away, say, being assertive

indicators.note: almost means the synonym stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to avert is to turn away, as one averts one's eyes

explanation.surface: Someone nearly looks away while speaking forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter T from AVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something firmly is to state it with assertion, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Work out, and chart pain of treatment without drugs

indicators.note: work as a verb tells us to work these letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient is told to exercise and plot their pain on a graph rather than take medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like exercise, but 'Work' is the anagram signal and OUT is part of the fodder with CHART PAIN; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturopathy is a system of healing by diet, herbs and natural means, avoiding medicinal drugs, so the adjective describes such care.

clue.text: Artist put up charges

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word put is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to put something is to set it down

explanation.surface: A painter raised the fees.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist; in a down clue 'up' reverses the word below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rates are fees or prices levied, so charges is a plain synonym.

clue.text: One may be needed after release prior to end of term

definitions.text: One may be needed after release prior to end of term

parts.words: One may be needed after release prior to end of term
parts.note: the release is a birth and the term is a pregnancy, so a premature baby is meant, not a prisoner or a schoolchild

explanation.surface: Someone let out of prison or school early may need help.
explanation.walkthrough: Release and term suggest prison or school, but they describe a baby born before full term, who is kept in a warm cot.
explanation.definitionFit: A premature baby is placed in a heated, enclosed hospital cot to keep it warm and safe.

clue.text: Foreign woman's almost complete deception

indicators.note: almost means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: a fraud is an outright deception or swindle

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad has very nearly pulled off a total con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the last letter D from FRAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German title and word for a married woman, so it is a woman from a foreign country.

clue.text: One puts pressure on, having needed dough, say

definitions.text: One puts pressure on, having needed dough, say

parts.words: One puts pressure on, having needed dough, say
parts.note: sounds like an extortioner short of money, but the dough is pastry already kneaded, now pressed flat

explanation.surface: A blackmailer leans on someone because they needed cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Dough is slang for money, and 'needed' sounds like kneaded: after kneading, pastry dough is flattened by pressing a roller over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylindrical kitchen roller presses pastry flat after the dough has been worked by hand.

clue.text: Replacement reporting to the boss and hearing why

parts.note: someone reporting to a superior works under them
a boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield

indicators.note: hearing tells us to take the letter that sounds like the word why

parts.note: the word why is said like the letter Y

explanation.surface: A stand-in answers to the manager and asks why at a disciplinary hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss is not a manager here: a boss is an ornamental knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy learns a role in order to replace the regular actor when needed.

clue.text: Split gear lever could be a dilemma

parts.note: cleft means split, as in a cleft chin
the gear lever in a car is commonly called the stick

explanation.surface: A broken gearshift could leave a driver in a quandary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a forked stick means being trapped between two difficult choices, so the phrase names a quandary.

clue.text: Walk from school around lake

indicators.note: around means the school word wraps the lake letter

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Pupils stroll from their school round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: School is not a place of learning but a group of whales, a POD.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to walk heavily and slowly, so it is a kind of walking.

clue.text: Maybe earwig sinister report of town near Gatwick?

parts.note: creepy means eerie or sinister

indicators.note: a report is a sound, so we want something said like the town

parts.note: Crawley is a town in West Sussex next to Gatwick Airport

explanation.surface: An earwig seems a sinister thing to find in a news report from a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Crawley is a West Sussex town beside Gatwick, London's second airport.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig is an example of a small insect or bug, which is informally called a creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Emergency measure keeping motorists on the way after a collision

definitions.text: Emergency measure keeping motorists on the way after a collision

parts.words: Emergency measure keeping motorists on the way after a collision
parts.note: suggests help sending drivers on their way after an accident, but describes a roadside safety rail that stops cars leaving the road

explanation.surface: Police take steps to keep traffic moving after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way' reads as continuing a journey but means staying on the road: the guardrail keeps a crashing car from leaving it.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside safety fence stops vehicles that collide with it from leaving the carriageway.

clue.text: Removed for not paying attention

explanation.surface: Someone was taken off the job for daydreaming.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both taken out or extracted, and absent-minded or preoccupied.

clue.text: Ship's officer selling great vehicle, when on leave

parts.note: super means great or excellent
a car is a vehicle
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A sailor sells off his fine car while on shore leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when on' is only a link; 'selling' belongs to the definition, since this officer handles the sale of cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercargo is a merchant ship's officer who manages the cargo and its sale on the owner's behalf.

clue.text: Unhappy with photo in plan

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
a print is a photographic copy

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy with the picture in their scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a technical drawing, and figuratively any detailed scheme for a project.

clue.text: At home, a gentle sort becomes less than couth

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mild person at home turns out to be uncouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' looks like scene-setting but supplies a piece; 'sort' is the anagram signal, and couth is a jokey back-formation from uncouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or refinement, an awkward manner is less than couth, the opposite of polished.

clue.text: Fungal infection acquired after ear's been cleared out

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first
the inside of the ear is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the word ear, the 's standing for has
got means acquired or obtained

explanation.surface: An infection was picked up after someone had their ears syringed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been cleared out' empties the ear, keeping only its first and last letters, and 'after' places the acquired word behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal disease of rye and other cereals, caused by a Claviceps fungus.

clue.text: Deal with junk found round about

indicators.note: round means the junk word encircles the about word

parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless rubbish
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A dealer handles rubbish discovered round the place.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a verb here, not a dealer's trade; 'round' is the container signal and 'found' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter or subject is to deal with or handle it.

clue.text: One dealing with matters arising sooner?

definitions.text: One dealing with matters arising sooner?

parts.words: One dealing with matters arising sooner?
parts.note: reads like an official handling business ahead of time, but means someone who gets out of bed early

explanation.surface: An efficient administrator deals with business before it comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matters arising' is a meeting agenda item; read literally it is the person getting up early.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for someone who rises early comes from the proverb about catching the worm.

clue.text: Teach recruit complex principles of design

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An instructor teaches a newcomer some complicated design theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and, more widely, any system's structure.

clue.text: Craftsman left during row

indicators.note: during means the left letter sits within the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A craftsman walked out in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Row is a line, TIER, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler is a tradesman who lays tiles on roofs, floors or walls.

clue.text: Bank right and see

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is one

explanation.surface: A banking instruction about what is correct and should be checked.
explanation.walkthrough: See is a bishop's seat; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to depend or count on it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Brought up talk of money

indicators.note: talk of means the word for money as spoken

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone was raised hearing about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means reared or raised, as in born and bred.

clue.text: Right account, but no heading

indicators.note: without its heading, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a story is an account of events

explanation.surface: A correct report that lacks a headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no heading' drops the S from STORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of the Conservative Party, the British political right.

clue.text: Wildlife that's somehow freed without permit

indicators.note: without means outside, so the anagram letters enclose the permit word
somehow says the word freed is arranged in some other way

parts.note: to allow is to permit

explanation.surface: Animals have been released without a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; 'somehow' rearranges freed to FDEER, which wraps the permit word.
explanation.definitionFit: This small deer is a wild animal, an example of the wildlife of British parks and woods.

clue.text: Condemn the return of the blues, perhaps

indicators.note: return means the word for the blues is read backwards

parts.note: the blues is a mood, so perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Critics denounce the revival of blues music.
explanation.walkthrough: The blues is a gloomy state of mind, a MOOD, and 'return of' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To doom someone is to condemn them to an unhappy fate.

clue.text: Visionary run into yesterday, eccentric

indicators.note: into means the run letter goes inside the rearranged letters
eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An idealist charges back into the past in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges YESTERDAY to STARYEYED, and R goes 'into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry-eyed means idealistic and dreamy, as a visionary person tends to be.
